notes:
Summary: mid-market PM + infra leads evaluating Hosted first (fast test) then move to Dedicated for cost predictability and isolation. PoC on hosted looked good for quality but unit cost variance is concern. Team wants Dedicated for stable per-token economics and VPC termination.

Key requirements / quotes: 
- "Cannot have model data leave our VPC" (infra lead) — strong push for VPC/Private networking.
- Latency target: p95 < 250ms for chat flows, p50 ~< 120ms desirable. Throughput: steady 40-60 rps; burst to 150 rps.
- Cost sensitivity: target ARR impact < 1.5% of GTM spend; looking for committed tiers + overage pricing clarity.

Legal/procurement items: 
- MSA redlines: cap on liability tied to fees, carveouts for security incidents, tighter definition of "Confidential Information".
- DPA redlines: data residency + subprocessors list required; retention windows spelled out (customer wants 90 days max for logs).
- SLA: request for 99.95% uptime, defined credits, and an escalation path into Redwood's on-call beyond basic support.
- Vendor onboarding: require SOC2 report, penetration test summary, KMS integration checklist, auditor access for limited time.

POC notes: 
- Hosted PoC ran on Redwood-hosted instance with default Llama-like model; accuracy uplift ~12% on retrieval QA.
- Cost: hosted token costs exceeded internal target by ~25% for peak workloads; Dedicated expected to lower unit cost but needs committed sizing.

Action items (short):
- Legal: counter redlines on MSA + produce DPA with residency options (AE to coordinate).
- SE: provide Dedicated capacity worksheet + quantized model perf numbers (Liam).
- Finance: send committed pricing spreadsheet and billing cadence options.
- Customer: confirm internal procurement timeline (expected sign-off by 2025-02).

Staging shorthand: "demo -> hosted PoC -> dedicated sizing -> legal redlines -> procurement".

Recent quote from Head of Product: "We need stable unit economics before we commit — if Dedicated gives that, we'll consolidate all inferencing there."
